<term_definitions code="at0000">
    <items id="text">Klinischer Status</items>
    <items id="description">Contextual or temporal qualifier for a specified problem or diagnosis.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0001">
    <items id="text">Episodicity</items>
    <items id="description">Category of this episode for the identified problem/diagnosis.</items>
    <items id="comment">For example: 'New' will enable clinicians to distinguish a new, acute episode of otitis media that may have arisen soon after a previous diagnosis, to distinguish it from an unresolved or 'Ongoing' diagnosis of chronic otitis media. Treatment of recurring, new and acute, episodes of a condition may differ significantly from the same condition that is not resolving or responding to treatment. In many situations the clinician will not be able to tell, and so indeterminate may be appropriate.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0003">
    <items id="text">Klinischer Status</items>
    <items id="description">Category that supports division of problems and diagnoses into Active or Inactive problem lists.</items>
    <items id="comment">The Active/Inactive and Current/Past data elements have similar clinical impact but represent slightly different semantics. Both are actively used in different clinical settings, but usually not together. If a Current/Past qualifier is recorded, then this data element is likely to be redundant. An exception where a condition can be current but inactive is asthma that is not causing acute symptoms.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0004">
    <items id="text">Diagnostic status</items>
    <items id="description">Stage or phase of diagnostic process.</items>
    <items id="comment">The status is usually determined by a combination of the timing of diagnosis plus level of clinical certainty resulting from diagnostic tests and clinical evidence available. This data element and 'Diagnostic certainty' in EVALUATION.problem_diagnosis are two important axes of the diagnostic process, and valid combinations will need to be presented by software that exposes both data elements, so it is not possible for users to select conflicting combinations. 
Preliminary or working diagnoses are intended to represent the single most likely choice out of all differential diagnosis options.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0016">
    <items id="text">Preliminary</items>
    <items id="description">The initial diagnosis made, usually associated with a low level of clinical certainty. It may change as test results or advice become available.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0017">
    <items id="text">Working</items>
    <items id="description">Interim diagnosis, based on a reasonable amount of clinical certainty but pending further test results or clinical advice. It may still change as test results or advice become available.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0018">
    <items id="text">Established</items>
    <items id="description">Final substantiated diagnosis, based on a high level of clinical certainty, which may include clinical evidence from test results. It is not expected to change.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0026">
    <items id="text">Active</items>
    <items id="description">The problem or diagnosis is currently active and clinically relevant.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0027">
    <items id="text">Inactive</items>
    <items id="description">The problem or diagnosis is not completely resolved but is inactive or felt less relevant to the current clinical context.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0034">
    <items id="text">New</items>
    <items id="description">A new occurrence of either a new or existing problem or diagnosis. A flag for 'First occurrence' can be recorded separately to distinguish the first from other occurrences.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0035">
    <items id="text">Ongoing</items>
    <items id="description">The issue, problem or diagnosis continues, without new, acute episodes occurring.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0060">
    <items id="text">Current/Past?</items>
    <items id="description">Category that supports division of problems and diagnoses into Current or Past problem lists.</items>
    <items id="comment">The Current/Past and Active/Inactive data elements have similar clinical impact but represent slightly different semantics. Both are actively used in different clinical settings, but usually not together. If an Active/Inactive qualifier is recorded, then this data element is likely to be redundant. An exception where a condition can be current but inactive is asthma that is not causing acute symptoms.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0061">
    <items id="text">Past</items>
    <items id="description">An issue which ocurred in the past.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0062">
    <items id="text">Current</items>
    <items id="description">An issue occuring at present.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0063">
    <items id="text">Diagnostic category</items>
    <items id="description">Category of the problem or diagnosis within a specified episode of care and/or local care context.</items>
    <items id="comment">This data element contains a value set commonly used in diagnostic categorisation. In episodic care contexts (commonly secondary care) it is common to categorise/organise diagnoses according to their relationship to the principal diagnosis being addressed during that episode of care. These categories may also be used for clinical coding, reporting and billing purposes. In some countries the diagnostic category may be known as a DRG.
 In addition, the free text choice permits use of other local value sets, as required.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0064">
    <items id="text">Principal diagnosis</items>
    <items id="description">The diagnosis determined to be the primary reason for an episode of admitted patient care, an episode of residential care or an attendance at the health care establishment.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0066">
    <items id="text">Secondary diagnosis</items>
    <items id="description">A problem or diagnosis that occurs at the same time as the primary problem or diagnosis. May also be known as a comorbid condition.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0070">
    <items id="text">Indeterminate</items>
    <items id="description">It is not possible to determine if this occurrence of the problem or diagnosis is new or ongoing.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0071">
    <items id="text">Occurrence</items>
    <items id="description">Category of the occurrence for this problem or diagnosis.</items>
    <items id="comment">This data element can be an additional qualifier to the 'New' value in the 'Episodicity' value set, that is a condition such as asthma can have recurring new episodes that have periods of resolution in between. However it can be important to identify the first ever episode of asthma from all of the other episodes.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0073">
    <items id="text">Admission diagnosis?</items>
    <items id="description">Was the problem or diagnosis present at admission?</items>
    <items id="comment">Record as True or 'Yes' if the problem or diagnosis was present on admission. This data element is a requirement from DRG reporting in some countries.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0076">
    <items id="text">Complication</items>
    <items id="description">An unfavorable evolution of a problem or diagnosis.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0077">
    <items id="text">Course label</items>
    <items id="description">Category reflecting the speed of onset and/or duration and persistence of the problem or diagnosis.</items>
    <items id="comment">Definitions of acute vs chronic will differ for each diagnosis.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0079">
    <items id="text">Chronic</items>
    <items id="description">A problem or diagnosis with persistent or long-lasting effects, or that evolves over time.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0081">
    <items id="text">Acute</items>
    <items id="description">A problem or diagnosis with a rapid onset, a short course, or both.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0083">
    <items id="text">Resolution phase</items>
    <items id="description">Phase of healing for an acute problem or diagnosis.</items>
    <items id="comment">For example: tracking the progress of resolution of a middle ear infection.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0084">
    <items id="text">Resolved</items>
    <items id="description">Problem or diagnosis has completed the normal phases of restoration or healing and can be considered resolved.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0085">
    <items id="text">Resolving</items>
    <items id="description">Problem or diagnosis is progressing satisfactorily through the normal stages of restoration or healing towards resolution.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0086">
    <items id="text">Not resolving</items>
    <items id="description">Problem or diagnosis is not progressing satisfactorily through the normal stages of restoration or healing towards resolution.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0087">
    <items id="text">Indeterminate</items>
    <items id="description">It is not possible to determine the resolution or healing status of the problem or diagnosis.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0088">
    <items id="text">Refuted</items>
    <items id="description">The previously recorded diagnosis has been clinically reassessed or disproved with a high level of clinical certainty. This status is used to correct an error in the health record.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0089">
    <items id="text">Remission status</items>
    <items id="description">Status of the remission of an incurable diagnosis.</items>
    <items id="comment">For example: the status of a cancer or haematological diagnosis.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0090">
    <items id="text">In remission</items>
    <items id="description">No ongoing signs or symptoms of the disease have been identified.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0092">
    <items id="text">Not in remission</items>
    <items id="description">No diminution of the signs or symptoms of the disease have been identified.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0093">
    <items id="text">Indeterminate</items>
    <items id="description">It is not possible to determine if there have been diminution of the signs or symptoms of the disease have been identified.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0094">
    <items id="text">Acute-on-chronic</items>
    <items id="description">A problem or diagnosis with an acute exacerbation of a chronic condition.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0095">
    <items id="text">First occurrence</items>
    <items id="description">This is the first ever occurrence of this problem or diagnosis.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0096">
    <items id="text">Recurrence</items>
    <items id="description">New occurrence of the same problem or diagnosis after a previous episode was resolved.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0097">
    <items id="text">Relapsed</items>
    <items id="description">Problem or diagnosis has deteriorated after a period of temporary improvement.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0098">
    <items id="text">Level of control</items>
    <items id="description">Category of the level of control of the problem or diagnosis by the current management.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0099">
    <items id="text">Controlled</items>
    <items id="description">The problem or diagnosis is controlled by current management.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0100">
    <items id="text">Indeterminate</items>
    <items id="description">It is not possible to determine if the problem or diagnosis is controlled by current management.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0101">
    <items id="text">Not controlled</items>
    <items id="description">The problem or diagnosis is not controlled by current management.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0102">
    <items id="text">Progression</items>
    <items id="description">Category of the progression through the course of a chronic problem or diagnosis.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0103">
    <items id="text">Improving</items>
    <items id="description">The problem or diagnosis is improving.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0104">
    <items id="text">Stable</items>
    <items id="description">The problem or diagnosis is unchanged.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0105">
    <items id="text">Worsening</items>
    <items id="description">The problem or diagnosis is worsening.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0106">
    <items id="text">Indeterminate</items>
    <items id="description">It is not possible to determine the progression of the problem or diagnosis.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0107">
    <items id="text">Reason for an ongoing episode</items>
    <items id="description">Reason for a problem or diagnosis not resolving as expected.</items>
    <items id="comment">For example: incomplete or failed treatment.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0108">
    <items id="text">Yes</items>
    <items id="description"></items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0109">
    <items id="text">No</items>
    <items id="description"></items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0110">
    <items id="text">Comment</items>
    <items id="description">Additional narrative about the Problem/Diagnosis qualifier values, not captured in other fields.</items>
</term_definitions>

                <term_definitions code="at0000">
                    <items id="text">Sekundärcode</items>
                    <items id="description">Details about a single identified health condition, injury, disability or any other issue which impacts on the physical, mental and/or social well-being of an individual.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Clear delineation between the scope of a problem versus a diagnosis is not easy to achieve in practice. For the purposes of clinical documentation with this archetype, problem and diagnosis are regarded as a continuum, with increasing levels of detail and supportive evidence usually providing weight towards the label of 'diagnosis'.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0001">
                    <items id="text">structure</items>
                    <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0002">
                    <items id="text">Kodierte Diagnose - icd-o-3</items>
                    <items id="description">Identification of the problem or diagnosis, by name.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Coding of the name of the problem or diagnosis with a terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0003">
                    <items id="text">Feststellungsdatum</items>
                    <items id="description">Estimated or actual date/time the diagnosis or problem was recognised by a healthcare professional.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Partial dates are acceptable. If the subject of care is under the age of one year, then the complete date or a minimum of the month and year is necessary to enable accurate age calculations - for example, if used to drive decision support. Data captured/imported as "Age at time of clinical recognition" should be converted to a date using the subject's date of birth.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0005">
                    <items id="text">Severity</items>
                    <items id="description">An assessment of the overall severity of the problem or diagnosis.</items>
                    <items id="comment">If severity is included in the Problem/diagnosis name via precoordinated codes, this data element becomes redundant. Note: more specific grading of severity can be recorded using the Specific details SLOT.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0009">
                    <items id="text">Freitextbeschreibung</items>
                    <items id="description">Narrative description about the problem or diagnosis.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Use to provide background and context, including evolution, episodes or exacerbations, progress and any other relevant details, about the problem or diagnosis.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0012">
                    <items id="text">Körperstelle - icd-o-3</items>
                    <items id="description">Identification of a simple body site for the location of the problem or diagnosis.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Coding of the name of the anatomical location with a terminology is preferred, where possible.
Use this data element to record precoordinated anatomical locations. If the requirements for recording the anatomical location are determined at run-time by the application or require more complex modelling such as relative locations then use the CLUSTER.anatomical_location or CLUSTER.relative_location within the 'Structured anatomical location' SLOT in this archetype. Occurrences for this data element are unbounded to allow for clinical scenarios such as describing a rash in multiple locations but where all of the other attributes are identical. If the anatomical location is included in the Problem/diagnosis name via precoordinated codes, this data element becomes redundant.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0030">
                    <items id="text">Klinisch relevanter Zeitraum (Zeitpunkt der Genesung)</items>
                    <items id="description">Estimated or actual date/time of resolution or remission for this problem or diagnosis, as determined by a healthcare professional.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Partial dates are acceptable. If the subject of care is under the age of one year, then the complete date or a minimum of the month and year is necessary to enable accurate age calculations - for example, if used to drive decision support. Data captured/imported as "Age at time of resolution" should be converted to a date using the subject's date of birth.
</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0032">
                    <items id="text">Tree</items>
                    <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0039">
                    <items id="text">Structured body site</items>
                    <items id="description">A structured anatomical location for the problem or diagnosis.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Use this SLOT to insert the CLUSTER.anatomical_location or CLUSTER.relative_location archetypes if the requirements for recording the anatomical location are determined at run-time by the application or require more complex modelling such as relative locations.

If the anatomical location is included in the Problem/diagnosis name via precoordinated codes, use of this SLOT becomes redundant.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0043">
                    <items id="text">Specific details</items>
                    <items id="description">Details that are additionally required to record as unique attributes of this problem or diagnosis.</items>
                    <items id="comment">May include structured detail about the grading or staging of the diagnosis; diagnostic criteria, classification criteria or formal severity assessments such as Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0046">
                    <items id="text">Status</items>
                    <items id="description">Structured details for location-, domain-, episode- or workflow-specific aspects of the diagnostic process.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Use status or context qualifiers with care, as they are variably used in practice and interoperability cannot be assured unless usage is clearly defined with the community of use. For example: active status - active, inactive, resolved, in remission; evolution status - initial, interim/working, final; temporal status - current, past; episodicity status - first, new, ongoing; admission status - admission, discharge; or priority status - primary, secondary.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0047">
                    <items id="text">Mild</items>
                    <items id="description">The problem or diagnosis does not interfere with normal activity or may cause damage to health if left untreated.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0048">
                    <items id="text">Moderate</items>
                    <items id="description">The problem or diagnosis causes interference with normal activity or will damage health if left untreated.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0049">
                    <items id="text">Severe</items>
                    <items id="description">The problem or diagnosis prevents normal activity or will seriously damage health if left untreated.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0069">
                    <items id="text">Diagnoseerläuterung</items>
                    <items id="description">Additional narrative about the problem or diagnosis not captured in other fields.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0070">
                    <items id="text">Letztes Dokumentationsdatum</items>
                    <items id="description">The date this problem or diagnosis was last updated.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0071">
                    <items id="text">Extension</items>
                    <items id="description">Additional information required to capture local content or to align with other reference models/formalisms.</items>
                    <items id="comment">For example: local information requirements or additional metadata to align with FHIR or CIMI equivalents.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0072">
                    <items id="text">Course description</items>
                    <items id="description">Narrative description about the course of the problem or diagnosis since onset.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0073">
                    <items id="text">Diagnosesicherheit</items>
                    <items id="description">The level of confidence in the identification of the diagnosis.</items>
                    <items id="comment">If an alternative valueset is required, these values can be added to the DV_TEXT data type in a template.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0074">
                    <items id="text">Suspected</items>
                    <items id="description">The diagnosis has been identified with a low level of certainty.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0075">
                    <items id="text">Probable</items>
                    <items id="description">The diagnosis has been identified with a high level of certainty.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0076">
                    <items id="text">Confirmed</items>
                    <items id="description">The diagnosis has been confirmed against recognised criteria.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0077">
                    <items id="text">Klinisch relevanter Zeitraum (Zeitpunkt des Auftretens)</items>
                    <items id="description">Estimated or actual date/time that signs or symptoms of the problem/diagnosis were first observed.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Data captured/imported as "Age at onset" should be converted to a date using the subject's date of birth.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0078">
                    <items id="text">Cause</items>
                    <items id="description">A cause, set of causes, or manner of causation of the problem or diagnosis.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Also known as 'aetiology' or 'etiology'. Coding with an external terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0079">
                    <items id="text">Variant</items>
                    <items id="description">Specific variant or subtype of the Diagnosis, if relevant.</items>
                    <items id="comment">For example: 'acute motor axonal neuropathy' as a variant of Guillain-Barre Syndrome. Coding of the name of the variant with a terminology is preferred, where possible. </items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="SNOMED CT::24484000">
                    <items id="text">Severe (severity modifier) (qualifier value)</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="SNOMED CT::6736007">
                    <items id="text">Moderate (severity modifier) (qualifier value)</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="SNOMED CT::255604002">

                </term_definitions>

        <term_definitions code="at0000">
            <items id="text">Specimen</items>
            <items id="description">A physical sample collected from, or related to, an individual for the purpose of investigation, examination or analysis.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: Tissue or body fluid.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0001">
            <items id="text">Laboratory specimen identifier</items>
            <items id="description">A unique identifier of the specimen, normally assigned by the laboratory.</items>
            <items id="comment">Sometimes called the Accession Identifier. Specimen containers, for example vacuum vials or tissue cassettes, have their own identitiers which may be recorded in the 'Container identifier' element in the 'Specimen container' archetype.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0003">
            <items id="text">Parent specimen identifier</items>
            <items id="description">Unique identifier of the parent specimen, where the specimen is split into sub-samples.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: A specific histology slide specimen can have a specific paraffin wax block as its parent specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0005">
            <items id="text">Hazard warning</items>
            <items id="description">Identified health risk or biohazard to the collector or laboratory staff due to exposure to, or contact with, the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: 'Hepatitis B'; "nerve agent'. Coding of the 'Hazard warning' with a terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0007">
            <items id="text">Collection method</items>
            <items id="description">The method of collection used.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: venepuncture, biopsy, resection. Coding of the collection method with a terminology is preferred, where possible. If the collection method is included in the 'Specimen type' via precoordinated codes, this data element becomes redundant.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0008">
            <items id="text">Sampling context</items>
            <items id="description">The context in which the specimen is collected.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: 'fasting'; 'full bladder'; 'sterile field'; or special instructions on the handling or immediate processing of the sample, such as 'centrifuge on receipt'. This data element also be used to document any known deviations from collection or handling instructions, for example that the patient had not fasted, even when this had been originally requested. Coding of the 'Sampling context' with a terminology is preferred, where possible.

If this archetype is used within an INSTRUCTION archetype, the context will reflect the intended or desired conditions at sample collection. If this archetype is used for representing an ACTION archetype pathway step which correlates with the collection being performed or completed, the context will be reflecting the conditions that existed at sample collection and this may also be copied to the 'Confounding factors' element of the OBSERVATION.laboratory_test_result archetype.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0013">
            <items id="text">Structured source site</items>
            <items id="description">A structured description of the area of the body from where the specimen is collected.</items>
            <items id="comment">Utilise the more detailed archetypes to describe structured or more complex anatomical sites, or to support recording the source site at run-time by the application. If the body site has been fully identified in the 'Source site' data element, this SLOT becomes redundant.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0015">
            <items id="text">Collection date/time</items>
            <items id="description">The date and time that collection has been ordered to take place or has taken place.</items>
            <items id="comment">This datetime will be captured primarily in the INSTRUCTION timing, ACTION time or OBSERVATION times. However, as this is a critical piece of information, it can be useful to also associate it directly with the specimen itself.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0027">
            <items id="text">Physical properties</items>
            <items id="description">Physical dimensions, mass or non-measurable properties of the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: Volume, mass, circumference, colour, smell, turbidity. This element can be used to specify the properties of the specimen to be collected, in the context of an INSTRUCTION archetype, or the properties of the specimen which was collected, in the context of an ACTION or OBSERVATION archetype. For example, an INSTRUCTION may request the collection of 20 ml of blood, while the corresponding ACTION records that only 15 ml was collected.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0029">
            <items id="text">Specimen type</items>
            <items id="description">The type of specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: Venous blood, bacterial culture, cytology, or tissue sample. Coding of the specimen type with a terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0034">
            <items id="text">Date/time received</items>
            <items id="description">The date and time that the sample was received at the laboratory.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0041">
            <items id="text">Adequacy for testing</items>
            <items id="description">Information about whether the specimen was adequate for testing.</items>
            <items id="comment">This element is intended to be used to record a judgement about whether or not the specimen quality was good enough for testing, and whether or not testing has been carried out. Coding of the specimen quality issues with a terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0042">
            <items id="text">Specimen quality issue</items>
            <items id="description">A specific quality issue with a specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">Coding of the specimen quality issues with a terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0045">
            <items id="text">Comment</items>
            <items id="description">Additional narrative about the specimen not captured in other fields.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0052">
            <items id="text">Haemolysed</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen was haemolysed.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0053">
            <items id="text">Lipaemic</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen was lipaemic.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0054">
            <items id="text">Incorrect additive</items>
            <items id="description">An incorrect additive such as a transport medium or preservative was added to the specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0055">
            <items id="text">Insufficient amount</items>
            <items id="description">The available amount of specimen was insufficient to undertake the examination.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0062">
            <items id="text">Satisfactory</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen is of sufficient quality to allow reporting.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0063">
            <items id="text">Unsatisfactory - analysed</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen is unsatisfactory but has been analysed.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0064">
            <items id="text">Unsatisfactory - not analysed</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen is unsatisfactory and has not been analysed.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0067">
            <items id="text">Collection setting</items>
            <items id="description">Identification of the physical setting in which the specimen is collected.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: laboratory outpatient clinic, at home, or hospital ward. This specifies the type of specimen collection location within the healthcare environment. The specimen collection setting may provide additional information relevant to the analysis of the result.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0068">
            <items id="text">Processing details</items>
            <items id="description">Structured details about preparation or processing of the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: Staining or fixation.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0070">
            <items id="text">Specimen collector identifier</items>
            <items id="description">Identifier of the person or organisation responsible for collecting the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">This element is intended to be used where the specimen has already been collected and the actual collector is known.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0071">
            <items id="text">Specimen collector details</items>
            <items id="description">The person or organisation responsible for collecting the specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0079">
            <items id="text">Collection description</items>
            <items id="description">Narrative description about the collection of the specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0080">
            <items id="text">Number of containers</items>
            <items id="description">The total number of physical units holding this specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: Number of buckets, jars, vials, tubes, blocks, slides or grids.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0083">
            <items id="text">Additional details</items>
            <items id="description">Additional structured details about the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: details about needle biopsies in prostate cancer, where both the request and reporting about the specimen are detailed and specific.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0085">
            <items id="text">Container details</items>
            <items id="description">Details about containers used.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0087">
            <items id="text">Source site</items>
            <items id="description">Identification of the body site or other location from where the specimen is collected.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: 'wound on left calf', 'IV cannula right arm', 'right kidney'.
Coding of the name of the source site with a terminology is preferred, where possible. Use this data element to record precoordinated source sites. If the requirements for recording the source site are determined at run-time by the application or require more complex modelling such as relative locations then use the 'Structured source site' SLOT in this archetype. If the source site is included in the 'Specimen type' via precoordinated codes, this data element becomes redundant.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0088">
            <items id="text">External identifier</items>
            <items id="description">A unique identifier of the specimen, assigned by a party external to the laboratory.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: 'Requester ID', 'Archive ID, 'Biobank ID'.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0089">
            <items id="text">Icteric</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen was icteric.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0090">
            <items id="text">Handling error</items>
            <items id="description">An error arose when handling the specimen. For example: Incorrect storage, broken container.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0091">
            <items id="text">Age</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen was too old to analyse or to analyse accurately.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0092">
            <items id="text">Technical failure</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen could not be analysed for technical reasons.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0093">
            <items id="text">Transport details</items>
            <items id="description">Structured details about transport of the specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0094">
            <items id="text">Clotted</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen was clotted.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0095">
            <items id="text">Incorrectly labelled</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen was labelled incorrectly.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0096">
            <items id="text">Digital representation</items>
            <items id="description">Structured details about a digital representation of the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example the scanned image of a histopathology slide.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0097">
            <items id="text">Specimen description</items>
            <items id="description">Narrative description about the specimen being examined.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: the color and viscosity of a liquid; the shape of a solid tissue; or a description of tissue fragments.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0098">
            <items id="text">Specimen label</items>
            <items id="description">A name or label describing the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">Usually only relevant for anatomical pathology samples. For example: 'Sigmoid resection with a piece of bladder wall' or 'Aggregate of multiple skin biopsy fragments'.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0099">
            <items id="text">Number of fragments</items>
            <items id="description">The number of tissue fragments comprising the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">Usually only relevant when a number of tissue fragments are being examined and reported on as a single specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0100">
            <items id="text">Storage details</items>
            <items id="description">Structured details about the storage of the specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>
    </children>

    <items id="text">Einsender</items>
    <items id="description">An entity comprising one or more people and having a particular purpose.</items>
    <items id="comment">For example: a company, institution, association, network, department, community group, healthcare practice group, payer/insurer, care team, or a group of neighbours who provide care or support.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0001">
    <items id="text">Name</items>
    <items id="description">The unstructured name or label for the organisation.</items>
    <items id="comment">For example: 'Royal Children's Hospital'; 'ABC District Nursing Service'; 'YNWA Oslo' or 'JB Smith Lawyers'.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0002">
    <items id="text">Contact person</items>
    <items id="description">Details about one or more people within the organisation.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0003">
    <items id="text">Identifier</items>
    <items id="description">Identifier associated with the organisation.</items>
    <items id="comment">Occurrences for this data element is set to 0..* to allow for more than one Identifier to be recorded. Note that the ID data type contains multiple subcomponents for recording the ID value, type, issuer and assigner.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0004">
    <items id="text">Role</items>
    <items id="description">The relationship or role of the organisation to the individual or subject of care.</items>
    <items id="comment">For example: oncologist; palliative care home nursing service; or informal support network.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0005">
    <items id="text">Address</items>
    <items id="description">Details about an address for the organisation.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0017">
    <items id="text">Additional details</items>

</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0019">
    <items id="text">Comment</items>
    <items id="description">Additional narrative about the organisation not captured in other fields.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0021">
    <items id="text">Parent organisation</items>
    <items id="description">A larger organisation of which this organisation is a child or subsidiary.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0022">
    <items id="text">Electronic communication</items>
    <items id="description">Details about one or more types of electronic communication for the organisation.</items>
</term_definitions>

                <term_definitions code="at0000">
                    <items id="text">Laborleistung</items>
                    <items id="description">Request for a health-related service or activity to be delivered by a clinician, organisation or agency.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0001">
                    <items id="text">Current Activity</items>
                    <items id="description">Current Activity.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0008">
                    <items id="text">Tree</items>
                    <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0009">
                    <items id="text">Tree</items>
                    <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0010">
                    <items id="text">Auftrags-ID des anfordernden/einsendenden Systems (PLAC)</items>
                    <items id="description">The local identifier assigned by the requesting clinical system.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Usually equivalent to the HL7 Placer Order Identifier.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0011">
                    <items id="text">Receiver order identifier</items>
                    <items id="description">The local identifier assigned to the request by the clinician or organisation receiving the request for service.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Usually equivalent to the HL7 Filler Order Identifier.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0040">
                    <items id="text">Service due</items>
                    <items id="description">The date/time, or acceptable interval of date/time, for provision of the service.</items>
                    <items id="comment">This data element allows for recording of the timing for a single service, either as a date and time, a date ranges or a text descriptor which can allow for 'next available. In practice, clinicians will often think in terms of ordering services as approximate timing, for example: review in 3 months, 6 months or 12 months. As clinical systems need more exact parameters to operate on, this '3 months' will usually be converted to an exact date 3 months from the date of recording and stored using this data element. If complex timing or sequences of timings are required, use the CLUSTER.service_direction archetype within the 'Complex timing' SLOT and this data element becomes redundant.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0062">
                    <items id="text">Reason for request</items>
                    <items id="description">A short phrase describing the reason for the request.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Coding of the 'Reason for request' with a coding system is desirable, if available. This data element allows multiple occurrences to enable the user to record a multiple responses, if required. For example: 'manage diabetes complications'.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0064">
                    <items id="text">Reason description</items>
                    <items id="description">Narrative description about the reason for request.</items>
                    <items id="comment">For example: 'The patient's diabetes has recently become more difficult to stabilise and renal function is deteriorating'.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0065">
                    <items id="text">Intent</items>
                    <items id="description">Description of the intent for the request.</items>
                    <items id="comment">For example: a referral to a specialist may have the intent of the specialist taking over responsibility for care of the patient, or it may be to provide a second opinion on treatment options. Coding of the 'Intent' with a coding system is desirable, if available. This data element allows multiple occurrences to enable the user to record a multiple responses, if required.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0068">
                    <items id="text">Urgency</items>
                    <items id="description">Urgency of the request for service.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Specific definitions of emergency and urgent will vary between clinical contexts, clinical systems and the nature of the request itself, so have not been defined in this archetype. If explicit timing is required then the Service period should be clearly stated.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0076">
                    <items id="text">Supplementary information</items>
                    <items id="description">Supplementary information will be following request.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Record as TRUE if additional information has been identified and will be forwarded when available. For example: pending test results.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0078">
                    <items id="text">Information description</items>
                    <items id="description">Description of the supplementary information.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0112">
                    <items id="text">Extension</items>
                    <items id="description">Additional information required to capture local content or to align with other reference models/formalisms.</items>
                    <items id="comment">For example: local information requirements or additional metadata to align with FHIR or CIMI equivalents.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0116">
                    <items id="text">Patient requirements</items>
                    <items id="description">Language, transport or other personal requirements to support the patient's attendance or participation in provision of the service.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0121">
                    <items id="text">Name der Laborleistung</items>
                    <items id="description">The name of the single service or activity requested.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Coding of the 'Service name' with a coding system is desirable, if available. For example: 'referral' to an endocrinologist for diabetes management.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0127">
                    <items id="text">Request status</items>
                    <items id="description">The status of the request for service as indicated by the requester.</items>
                    <items id="comment">Status is used to denote whether this is the initial request, or a follow-up request to change or provide supplementary information. Coding with a terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0128">
                    <items id="text">Distribution list</items>
                    <items id="description">Details of additional clinicians, organisations or agencies who require copies of any communication.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0132">
                    <items id="text">Specific details</items>
                    <items id="description">Additional detail about the service requested.</items>
                    <items id="comment">For example: Specimen details for a laboratory test request, or anatomical location for a procedure request.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0135">
                    <items id="text">Description</items>
                    <items id="description">Narrative description about the service requested.</items>
                    <items id="comment">This data point should be used to describe the named service in more detail, including how it should be delivered, patient concerns and issues that might be encountered in delivering the service.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0136">
                    <items id="text">Emergency</items>
                    <items id="description">The request requires immediate attention.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0137">
                    <items id="text">Urgent</items>
                    <items id="description">The request requires prioritised attention.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0138">
                    <items id="text">Routine</items>
                    <items id="description">The request does not require prioritised scheduling.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0141">
                    <items id="text">Requester</items>
                    <items id="description">Details about the clinician or organisation requesting the service.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0142">
                    <items id="text">Receiver</items>
                    <items id="description">Details about the clinician or organisation receiving the request for service.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0144">
                    <items id="text">Service period expiry</items>
                    <items id="description">The date/time that marks the conclusion of the clinically valid period of time for delivery of this service.</items>
                    <items id="comment">This date/time is the equivalent to the latest possible date for service delivery or to the date of expiry for this request. For example: a service may be required to be completed before another event, such as scheduled surgery.</items>
                </term_definitions>
                <term_definitions code="at0145">

fhir:
  resourceType: "Bundle"
  condition:
    targetRoot: "$fhirResource"
    targetAttribute: "entry.resource.meta.profile"
    operator: "one of"
    criteria: "[https://www.medizininformatik-initiative.de/fhir/core/modul-labor/StructureDefinition/ServiceRequestLab]"

format: "0.2.0"
version: "0.0.1"

fhirConfig:
  resource: "ServiceRequest"
  multiple: false
openEhrConfig:
  archetype: "openEHR-EHR-INSTRUCTION.service_request.v1"

mappings:
  - name: "identifier"
    with:
      fhir: "$fhirResource.identifier"
      openehr: "$openEhrArchetype.laborleistung"
      type: "NONE"
    followedBy:
      mappings:
        - name: "identifier value"
          with:
            fhir: "value"
            openehr: "receiver_order_identifier.text_value"
            type: "STRING"
        - name: "identifier type"
          with:
            fhir: "type.coding.code"
            openehr: "auftrags-id_des_anfordernden_einsendenden_systems_plac|id"
            type: "STRING"

  - name: "status"
    with:
      fhir: "$fhirResource.status"
      openehr: "$openEhrArchetype.laborleistung.request_status"
      type: "CODING"

  - name: "code"
    with:
      fhir: "$fhirResource.code"
      openehr: "$openEhrArchetype.laborleistung.current_activity.name_der_laborleistung"
      type: "CODEABLECONCEPT"
  - name: "category"
    with:
      fhir: "$fhirResource.category"
      openehr: "$openEhrArchetype.laborleistung.current_activity.art_der_laborleistung_kategorie"
      type: "CODEABLECONCEPT"
  - name: "intent"
    with:
      fhir: "$fhirResource.intent"
      openehr: "$openEhrArchetype.laborleistung.current_activity.intent"
      type: "CODING"

  - name: "note"
    with:
      fhir: "$fhirResource.note.text"
      openehr: "$openEhrArchetype.laborleistung.current_activity.comment"
      type: "STRING"


  - name: "organisation"
    with:
      fhir: "$fhirResource.requester.as(Organization)"
      openehr: "$reference"
      type: "NONE"
    reference:
      resourceType: "Organization"
      mappings:
        - name: "org"
          with:
            fhir: "$fhirRoot"
            openehr: "$openEhrArchetype.laborleistung.einsender"
            type: "NONE"
          followedBy:
            mappings:
              - name: "org name"
                with:
                  fhir: "name"
                  openehr: "name"
                  type: "TEXT"
              - name: "org id"
                with:
                  fhir: "identifier"
                  openehr: "identifier"
                  type: "IDENTIFIER"



  - name: "specimen"
    with:
      fhir: "$fhirResource.specimen"
      openehr: "$reference"
      type: "NONE"
    reference:
      resourceType: "Specimen"
      mappings:
        - name: "specimen recurring"
          with:
            fhir: "$fhirRoot"
            openehr: "$openEhrArchetype.laborleistung.current_activity.specimen" # you need to do this because specimen is recurring element in openehr
            type: "NONE"
          followedBy:
            mappings:
              - name: "specimen identifier"
                with:
                  fhir: "identifier"
                  openehr: "laboratory_specimen_identifier"
                  type: "IDENTIFIER"
              - name: "specimen collection"
                with:
                  fhir: "collection"
                  openehr: "$openEhrArchetype"
                  type: "NONE"
                followedBy:
                  mappings:
                    - name: "specimen collection date time"
                      with:
                        fhir: "collected.as(DateTimeType)"
                        openehr: "collection_date_time.date_time_value"
                        type: "DATETIME"
                    - name: "specimen collector"
                      with:
                        fhir: "collector.as(Reference).identifier" # if you don't explicitly cast to Reference, it will try to add a Resource
                        openehr: "specimen_collector_identifier"
                        type: "IDENTIFIER"

        <term_definitions code="at0000">
            <items id="text">Specimen</items>
            <items id="description">A physical sample collected from, or related to, an individual for the purpose of investigation, examination or analysis.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: Tissue or body fluid.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0001">
            <items id="text">Laboratory specimen identifier</items>
            <items id="description">A unique identifier of the specimen, normally assigned by the laboratory.</items>
            <items id="comment">Sometimes called the Accession Identifier. Specimen containers, for example vacuum vials or tissue cassettes, have their own identitiers which may be recorded in the 'Container identifier' element in the 'Specimen container' archetype.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0003">
            <items id="text">Parent specimen identifier</items>
            <items id="description">Unique identifier of the parent specimen, where the specimen is split into sub-samples.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: A specific histology slide specimen can have a specific paraffin wax block as its parent specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0005">
            <items id="text">Hazard warning</items>
            <items id="description">Identified health risk or biohazard to the collector or laboratory staff due to exposure to, or contact with, the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: 'Hepatitis B'; "nerve agent'. Coding of the 'Hazard warning' with a terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0007">
            <items id="text">Collection method</items>
            <items id="description">The method of collection used.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: venepuncture, biopsy, resection. Coding of the collection method with a terminology is preferred, where possible. If the collection method is included in the 'Specimen type' via precoordinated codes, this data element becomes redundant.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0008">
            <items id="text">Sampling context</items>
            <items id="description">The context in which the specimen is collected.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: 'fasting'; 'full bladder'; 'sterile field'; or special instructions on the handling or immediate processing of the sample, such as 'centrifuge on receipt'. This data element also be used to document any known deviations from collection or handling instructions, for example that the patient had not fasted, even when this had been originally requested. Coding of the 'Sampling context' with a terminology is preferred, where possible.

If this archetype is used within an INSTRUCTION archetype, the context will reflect the intended or desired conditions at sample collection. If this archetype is used for representing an ACTION archetype pathway step which correlates with the collection being performed or completed, the context will be reflecting the conditions that existed at sample collection and this may also be copied to the 'Confounding factors' element of the OBSERVATION.laboratory_test_result archetype.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0013">
            <items id="text">Structured source site</items>
            <items id="description">A structured description of the area of the body from where the specimen is collected.</items>
            <items id="comment">Utilise the more detailed archetypes to describe structured or more complex anatomical sites, or to support recording the source site at run-time by the application. If the body site has been fully identified in the 'Source site' data element, this SLOT becomes redundant.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0015">
            <items id="text">Collection date/time</items>
            <items id="description">The date and time that collection has been ordered to take place or has taken place.</items>
            <items id="comment">This datetime will be captured primarily in the INSTRUCTION timing, ACTION time or OBSERVATION times. However, as this is a critical piece of information, it can be useful to also associate it directly with the specimen itself.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0027">
            <items id="text">Physical properties</items>
            <items id="description">Physical dimensions, mass or non-measurable properties of the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: Volume, mass, circumference, colour, smell, turbidity. This element can be used to specify the properties of the specimen to be collected, in the context of an INSTRUCTION archetype, or the properties of the specimen which was collected, in the context of an ACTION or OBSERVATION archetype. For example, an INSTRUCTION may request the collection of 20 ml of blood, while the corresponding ACTION records that only 15 ml was collected.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0029">
            <items id="text">Specimen type</items>
            <items id="description">The type of specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: Venous blood, bacterial culture, cytology, or tissue sample. Coding of the specimen type with a terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0034">
            <items id="text">Date/time received</items>
            <items id="description">The date and time that the sample was received at the laboratory.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0041">
            <items id="text">Adequacy for testing</items>
            <items id="description">Information about whether the specimen was adequate for testing.</items>
            <items id="comment">This element is intended to be used to record a judgement about whether or not the specimen quality was good enough for testing, and whether or not testing has been carried out. Coding of the specimen quality issues with a terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0042">
            <items id="text">Specimen quality issue</items>
            <items id="description">A specific quality issue with a specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">Coding of the specimen quality issues with a terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0045">
            <items id="text">Comment</items>
            <items id="description">Additional narrative about the specimen not captured in other fields.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0052">
            <items id="text">Haemolysed</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen was haemolysed.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0053">
            <items id="text">Lipaemic</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen was lipaemic.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0054">
            <items id="text">Incorrect additive</items>
            <items id="description">An incorrect additive such as a transport medium or preservative was added to the specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0055">
            <items id="text">Insufficient amount</items>
            <items id="description">The available amount of specimen was insufficient to undertake the examination.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0062">
            <items id="text">Satisfactory</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen is of sufficient quality to allow reporting.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0063">
            <items id="text">Unsatisfactory - analysed</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen is unsatisfactory but has been analysed.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0064">
            <items id="text">Unsatisfactory - not analysed</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen is unsatisfactory and has not been analysed.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0067">
            <items id="text">Collection setting</items>
            <items id="description">Identification of the physical setting in which the specimen is collected.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: laboratory outpatient clinic, at home, or hospital ward. This specifies the type of specimen collection location within the healthcare environment. The specimen collection setting may provide additional information relevant to the analysis of the result.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0068">
            <items id="text">Processing details</items>
            <items id="description">Structured details about preparation or processing of the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: Staining or fixation.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0070">
            <items id="text">Specimen collector identifier</items>
            <items id="description">Identifier of the person or organisation responsible for collecting the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">This element is intended to be used where the specimen has already been collected and the actual collector is known.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0071">
            <items id="text">Specimen collector details</items>
            <items id="description">The person or organisation responsible for collecting the specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0079">
            <items id="text">Collection description</items>
            <items id="description">Narrative description about the collection of the specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0080">
            <items id="text">Number of containers</items>
            <items id="description">The total number of physical units holding this specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: Number of buckets, jars, vials, tubes, blocks, slides or grids.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0083">
            <items id="text">Additional details</items>
            <items id="description">Additional structured details about the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: details about needle biopsies in prostate cancer, where both the request and reporting about the specimen are detailed and specific.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0085">
            <items id="text">Container details</items>
            <items id="description">Details about containers used.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0087">
            <items id="text">Source site</items>
            <items id="description">Identification of the body site or other location from where the specimen is collected.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: 'wound on left calf', 'IV cannula right arm', 'right kidney'.
Coding of the name of the source site with a terminology is preferred, where possible. Use this data element to record precoordinated source sites. If the requirements for recording the source site are determined at run-time by the application or require more complex modelling such as relative locations then use the 'Structured source site' SLOT in this archetype. If the source site is included in the 'Specimen type' via precoordinated codes, this data element becomes redundant.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0088">
            <items id="text">External identifier</items>
            <items id="description">A unique identifier of the specimen, assigned by a party external to the laboratory.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: 'Requester ID', 'Archive ID, 'Biobank ID'.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0089">
            <items id="text">Icteric</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen was icteric.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0090">
            <items id="text">Handling error</items>
            <items id="description">An error arose when handling the specimen. For example: Incorrect storage, broken container.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0091">
            <items id="text">Age</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen was too old to analyse or to analyse accurately.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0092">
            <items id="text">Technical failure</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen could not be analysed for technical reasons.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0093">
            <items id="text">Transport details</items>
            <items id="description">Structured details about transport of the specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0094">
            <items id="text">Clotted</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen was clotted.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0095">
            <items id="text">Incorrectly labelled</items>
            <items id="description">The specimen was labelled incorrectly.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0096">
            <items id="text">Digital representation</items>
            <items id="description">Structured details about a digital representation of the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example the scanned image of a histopathology slide.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0097">
            <items id="text">Specimen description</items>
            <items id="description">Narrative description about the specimen being examined.</items>
            <items id="comment">For example: the color and viscosity of a liquid; the shape of a solid tissue; or a description of tissue fragments.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0098">
            <items id="text">Specimen label</items>
            <items id="description">A name or label describing the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">Usually only relevant for anatomical pathology samples. For example: 'Sigmoid resection with a piece of bladder wall' or 'Aggregate of multiple skin biopsy fragments'.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0099">
            <items id="text">Number of fragments</items>
            <items id="description">The number of tissue fragments comprising the specimen.</items>
            <items id="comment">Usually only relevant when a number of tissue fragments are being examined and reported on as a single specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>
        <term_definitions code="at0100">
            <items id="text">Storage details</items>
            <items id="description">Structured details about the storage of the specimen.</items>
        </term_definitions>

<term_definitions code="at0000">
    <items id="text">Einsender</items>
    <items id="description">An entity comprising one or more people and having a particular purpose.</items>
    <items id="comment">For example: a company, institution, association, network, department, community group, healthcare practice group, payer/insurer, care team, or a group of neighbours who provide care or support.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0001">
    <items id="text">Name</items>
    <items id="description">The unstructured name or label for the organisation.</items>
    <items id="comment">For example: 'Royal Children's Hospital'; 'ABC District Nursing Service'; 'YNWA Oslo' or 'JB Smith Lawyers'.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0002">
    <items id="text">Contact person</items>
    <items id="description">Details about one or more people within the organisation.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0003">
    <items id="text">Identifier</items>
    <items id="description">Identifier associated with the organisation.</items>
    <items id="comment">Occurrences for this data element is set to 0..* to allow for more than one Identifier to be recorded. Note that the ID data type contains multiple subcomponents for recording the ID value, type, issuer and assigner.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0004">
    <items id="text">Role</items>
    <items id="description">The relationship or role of the organisation to the individual or subject of care.</items>
    <items id="comment">For example: oncologist; palliative care home nursing service; or informal support network.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0005">
    <items id="text">Address</items>
    <items id="description">Details about an address for the organisation.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0017">
    <items id="text">Additional details</items>
    <items id="description">Additional details about the organisation.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0019">
    <items id="text">Comment</items>
    <items id="description">Additional narrative about the organisation not captured in other fields.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0021">
    <items id="text">Parent organisation</items>
    <items id="description">A larger organisation of which this organisation is a child or subsidiary.</items>
</term_definitions>
<term_definitions code="at0022">
    <items id="text">Electronic communication</items>
    <items id="description">Details about one or more types of electronic communication for the organisation.</items>
</term_definitions>
